title: dual-path-token-rate-evaluation-with-elastic-stream-minimums-pilot
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Run a controlled pilot to evaluate a dual-path per-token billing model that separates ingress (input) and egress (output) token rates and introduces an elastic minimum for streaming sessions. The goal is to find a pricing configuration that (1) better aligns revenue with server-side cost for high-output streaming sessions, (2) preserves low-cost behaviour for read-heavy requests, and (3) surfaces a simple enterprise contract language for minimums and burst credits.

Background: Existing hosted API pricing ties a single per-token rate to requests with optional streaming. Customers and sales have asked for more predictable economics for high-output chat and long-generation use cases. Engineering has signalled that sustained streaming output creates disproportionate tail cost because of KV-cache retention and slower kernel paths. We need a small-scale experiment to determine how splitting input/output rates plus an elastic streaming minimum affects usage, revenue, and customer satisfaction.

Scope: Pilot will cover new customers and a subset of existing customers (opt-in) across three experiment arms: control (current unified rate), split-rate (separate ingress/egress rates, no minimum), and split+elastic-minimum (split rates + streaming minimum that scales with average session length). Work includes billing engine flag, telemetry, console indicators for customers, updated contract language draft for Sales, and a security questionnaire note for enterprise minimums.

Non-goals: Do not change Dedicated/Private pricing in this pilot. This is not a full commercial rollout; aim is to gather signal for an eventual proposal to leadership.
acceptance_criteria: Billing: Billing engine can apply separate ingress and egress per-token rates via a feature flag for test accounts without impacting existing customers.
Minimums: Billing supports an ‘elastic streaming minimum’ rule that charges a small flat minimum scaled by average session output for flagged accounts.
Telemetry: Dashboards track revenue per-session, tokens_in, tokens_out, average session length, churn for test cohort, and cost-per-session approximation.
Experiment: Run pilot for 6 weeks with at least 1000 sessions across cohorts; collect statistical signal on revenue lift and change in median latency/cost for egress-heavy sessions.

Contract docs: Draft contract clause for Sales + Legal explaining minimums, burst credits, and graceful backoff policies; security questionnaire language prepared for enterprise procurement responses.
Rollout safety: Fall-back policy implemented to revert flagged accounts to control within 1 hour in case of billing regressions.
Stakeholder signoff: Finance, Legal, and Platform Reliability must approve sample invoices and rollback plan prior to live testing.
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created; initial scope and hypothesis documented. Reached out to Billing (ENG-4210) to confirm feasibility of a per-path flag.
2025-02-14: Engineering feasibility spike accepted: ENG-4210 to implement billing flag; ENG-4372 to add session-level metrics. Estimate updated to 5 points.
2025-02-17: Sales and Legal sync — Sales requests explicit language for enterprise minimums and a sample amendment; Legal requests concrete rollback remediation and audit trail for invoices.

2025-02-20: Telemetry plan drafted; added dashboards and alert thresholds. Security: draft QA language added for enterprise questionnaires referencing minimums and data retention during long streaming sessions. Planning to start internal dogfood week starting 2025-03-03.
comments: Noah Kim (Eng): Need to validate that egress billing doesn't double-count tokens when streaming chunked responses. Suggested a short spike to instrument token attribution (linked).
Priya Gupta (Finance): Prefer experiment to run under feature-flagged accounts with synthetic invoice generation to validate revenue recognition mechanics before exposing to customers.
Evan Torres (Sales): Recommend offering an ‘introductory burst credit’ for enterprise pilots to soften adoption friction; Legal will define how credits show up on contract.
Aisha Patel (PM): We'll draft a simple customer-facing FAQ explaining why minimums exist and how burst credits work. Aim to keep messaging developer-friendly and explicit about when minimums apply.
